papers.title: On the Generalization of Learning-based 3D Reconstruction
alternate_titles: On the Generalization of Learning-based 3D Reconstruction
papers.abstract: State-of-the-art learning-based monocular 3D reconstruction methods learn priors over object categories on the training set, and as a result struggle to achieve reasonable generalization to object categories unseen during training. In this paper we study the inductive biases encoded in the model architecture that impact the generalization of learning-based 3D reconstruction methods. papers.title: Improving Human-Labeled Data through Dynamic Automatic Conflict Resolution
alternate_titles: Improving Human-Labeled Data through Dynamic Automatic Conflict Resolution
papers.abstract: This paper develops and implements a scalable methodology for (a) estimating the noisiness of labels produced by a typical crowdsourcing semantic annotation task, and (b) reducing the resulting error of the labeling process by as much as 20-30% in comparison to other common labeling strategies. Importantly, this new approach to the labeling process, which we name Dynamic Automatic Conflict Resolution (DACR), does not require a ground truth...

papers.title: What Neural Networks Memorize and Why: Discovering the Long Tail via Influence Estimation
alternate_titles: What Neural Networks Memorize and Why: Discovering the Long Tail via Influence Estimation
papers.abstract: Deep learning algorithms are well-known to have a propensity for fitting the training data very well and often fit even outliers and mislabeled data points. Such fitting requires memorization of training data labels, a phenomenon that has attracted significant research interest but has not been given a compelling explanation so far. papers.title: Stochastic Optimization with Laggard Data Pipelines
alternate_titles: Stochastic Optimization with Laggard Data Pipelines
papers.abstract: State-of-the-art optimization is steadily shifting towards massively parallel pipelines with extremely large batch sizes. papers.title: Stability of Stochastic Gradient Descent on Nonsmooth Convex Losses
alternate_titles: Stability of Stochastic Gradient Descent on Nonsmooth Convex Losses
papers.abstract: Uniform stability is a notion of algorithmic stability that bounds the worst case change in the model output by the algorithm when a single data point in the dataset is replaced. An influential work of Hardt et al. (2016) provides strong upper bounds on the uniform stability of the stochastic gradient descent (SGD) algorithm on sufficiently smooth convex losses. papers.title: Representing and Denoising Wearable ECG Recordings
alternate_titles: Representing and Denoising Wearable ECG Recordings
papers.abstract: Modern wearable devices are embedded with a range of noninvasive biomarker sensors that hold promise for improving detection and treatment of disease. One such sensor is the single-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) which measures electrical signals in the heart. papers.title: On the Error Resistance of Hinge-Loss Minimization
alternate_titles: On the Error Resistance of Hinge-Loss Minimization
papers.abstract: Commonly used classification algorithms in machine learning, such as support vector machines, minimize a convex surrogate loss on training examples. In practice, these algorithms are surprisingly robust to errors in the training data. In this work, we identify a set of conditions on the data under which such surrogate loss minimization algorithms provably learn the correct classifier. papers.title: Faster Differentially Private Samplers via Rényi Divergence Analysis of Discretized Langevin MCMC
alternate_titles: Faster Differentially Private Samplers via Rényi Divergence Analysis of Discretized Langevin MCMC
papers.abstract: Various differentially private algorithms instantiate the exponential mechanism, and require sampling from the distribution $exp(−f)$ for a suitable function $f$. When the domain of the distribution is high-dimensional, this sampling can be computationally challenging. papers.title: Collegial Ensembles
papers.abstract: Modern neural network performance typically improves as model size increases. A recent line of research on the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) of over-parameterized networks indicates that the improvement with size increase is a product of a better conditioned loss landscape.
